title: mcp-pinot -- T1190 unauthenticated 0.0.0.0 bind confused-deputy Pinot cluster access
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-49257 (GHSA-73cv-556c-w3g6,
CVSS 10.0 CRITICAL), a self-reported advisory for `mcp-pinot`, a
Python-based MCP server for Apache Pinot.

Versions 3.0.1 and below defaulted `oauth_enabled` to `False` and bound
the HTTP MCP server to `0.0.0.0:8080` -- reachable from any
network-adjacent caller, not just localhost. With OAuth disabled, FastMCP
registers every tool with no authentication check at all. The server then
proxies each call using its OWN server-side Pinot credentials
(`PINOT_TOKEN` or `PINOT_USERNAME`/`PINOT_PASSWORD`) rather than any
caller identity -- a textbook confused-deputy: the unauthenticated
network caller inherits the SERVER's privileges against the Pinot
cluster, not their own (they have none). Reachable tools include
`read_query` (arbitrary SELECT against any table), `create_schema` /
`update_schema`, and `create_table_config` / `update_table_config` --
full read/write access to the configured cluster.

This is a different failure shape than this corpus's other unauthenticated-
MCP-endpoint rules (`observed_ruflo_mcp_bridge_unauth_terminal_execute_t1190`,
`observed_whatsapp_mcp_bridge_path_traversal_t1005`): those exploit a
MISSING check on an otherwise-scoped API; this one exploits a working
auth toggle that is simply OFF by default, combined with a non-loopback
bind -- the server was never confused about auth existing, it just never
required it. Detection logic therefore keys on the specific mutation-tool
names reaching the wire without an Authorization header, rather than a
generic "MCP endpoint hit".

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (startreedata, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 3.1.0 (binds to `127.0.0.1` and rejects
non-loopback access without OAuth).
